correctness.rationale: For the finite language C(w) of distinct conjugates of w=10^a10^b, a complete minimal DFA has one dead quotient and nonempty quotients segregated by prefix length and number of consumed ones. Let ell=min(a,b), h=max(a,b), d=h−ell. All-zero prefixes contribute h+1 quotients, two-one prefixes another h+1. One-one prefixes 0^i1 0^j are feasible exactly in the union [0,ell]×[0,h] ∪ [0,h]×[0,ell], cardinality (ell+1)(2h−ell+1). Quotient collisions can only pair singleton A-only and B-only continuations, requiring i'=i+d, j'=j−d in min(d,ell+1)² distinct disjoint pairs. Thus the exact Myhill–Nerode quotient count is (2ell+4)h+4−ell²−min(d²,(ell+1)²), including equal gaps and adjacent ones. Independently enumerated complete right-quotient sets for 91 pairs 0≤a≤b≤12; every result matched. This checks finite instances only, with all-parameter proof from the rectangle and collision argument.
residual_risks: Distinct rotations, rather than rotation multiplicities, are the language; complete DFA includes one dead state.
Finite enumeration only verifies 91 parameter pairs and does not establish the unbounded formula by itself.

value.rationale: Exact complete DFA state count over every binary two-one cyclic-word language is a natural sharp descriptional-complexity classification. It tracks the nontrivial quotient mergers at h−ell=ell+1 and covers periodic degenerate equal gaps, supplying information not entailed by global extremal bounds.
residual_risks: Scope is precisely two marked bits and complete deterministic automata; no higher-marker or NFA complexity claim.

limitations: Other alphabets, ≥3 one-bits and nondeterministic complexity not assessed; older special-case literature partially inaccessible.
